items.q: The graph shows <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'</annotation></semantics></math>, the derivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math>. Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">″</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f''(1)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(1)</annotation></semantics></math>, the height of the graph. <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">″</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f''(1)</annotation></semantics></math> is its slope there.

items.q: On which interval is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">″</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f''(x) < 0</annotation></semantics></math>?

What can be said about <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">″</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f''(2)</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: It equals <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-2</annotation></semantics></math>, the value of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(2)</annotation></semantics></math>

It does not exist, because the graph of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'</annotation></semantics></math> has a corner at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 2</annotation></semantics></math>

It equals 0, because the graph of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'</annotation></semantics></math> turns around
It equals 2, the slope just to the right of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 2</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Let <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(x) = x f'(x)</annotation></semantics></math>. Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h'(4)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: The product rule has two terms; the first, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 \cdot f'(4) = 2</annotation></semantics></math>, is missing.

That is only <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(4)</annotation></semantics></math>. Add <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">″</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x f''(x) = 4 \cdot 2</annotation></semantics></math> from the product rule.

items.q: Differentiate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2 + 4y^2 = 8</annotation></semantics></math> implicitly to get the first derivative <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx}</annotation></semantics></math>, which the second derivative will need.

mistakes.why: The derivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4y^2</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>8</mn><mi>y</mi><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8y\frac{dy}{dx}</annotation></semantics></math>; the factor 4 stays.
Moving <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x</annotation></semantics></math> across the equals sign makes it negative.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}</annotation></semantics></math> at the point <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2, 1)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That treats <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> as a constant when differentiating <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>y</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{x}{4y}</annotation></semantics></math>. The quotient rule needs <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d}{dx}(4y) = 4\frac{dy}{dx}</annotation></semantics></math>.

The quotient rule's numerator is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(4y)(1) - x\left(4\frac{dy}{dx}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> makes the second term <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+4</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-4</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Using <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>y</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{x}{4y}</annotation></semantics></math> and the equation of the curve, which expression equals <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}</annotation></semantics></math>?

After differentiating <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>y</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{x}{4y}</annotation></semantics></math> with the quotient rule, a <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx}</annotation></semantics></math> appears in the result. What is the next step?
options: Replace it with 0, since it is a first derivative
Differentiate the result a third time

Replace it with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>y</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{x}{4y}</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Let <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = x^4 - 2x^3 + x</annotation></semantics></math>. Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">″</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f''(x)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(x)</annotation></semantics></math>. Differentiate once more.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">‴</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'''(x)</annotation></semantics></math>, one derivative too many.

items.q: Let <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = \sin(3x)</annotation></semantics></math>. Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">″</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f''(x)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: Both derivatives need the chain rule factor 3: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3 \cdot 3 = 9</annotation></semantics></math>.

The derivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos(3x)</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-3\sin(3x)</annotation></semantics></math>, so the sign is negative.

expr.answerHtml: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>9</mn><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-9\,\sin(3x)</annotation></semantics></math>

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx} = 2x \cdot e^{x^2}</annotation></semantics></math> is a product; the term from differentiating <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x</annotation></semantics></math>, which is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>e</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2e^{x^2}</annotation></semantics></math>, is missing.

The product rule has a second term: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x</annotation></semantics></math> times the derivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{x^2}</annotation></semantics></math>, which is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mi>e</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4x^2e^{x^2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Let <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = \ln x</annotation></semantics></math>. Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">‴</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'''(2)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: The power rule on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-x^{-2}</annotation></semantics></math> brings down <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-2</annotation></semantics></math>: the third derivative is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x^{-3}</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{-3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">″</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f''(2)</annotation></semantics></math>. Differentiate once more: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d}{dx}(-x^{-2}) = 2x^{-3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Which expression means the second derivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> with respect to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>?

Let <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = e^{-2x}</annotation></semantics></math>. Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{(5)}(0)</annotation></semantics></math>, the fifth derivative at 0.

mistakes.why: Five factors of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-2</annotation></semantics></math> give a negative number: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>5</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(-2)^5 = -32</annotation></semantics></math>.

The factors multiply, not add: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>5</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(-2)^5</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5(-2)</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: If <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(x) = x^2e^x</annotation></semantics></math>, find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">″</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f''(1)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is only <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2xe^x</annotation></semantics></math>; the product rule adds <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2e^x = e</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(1)</annotation></semantics></math>. Differentiate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'</annotation></semantics></math> once to get <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">″</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f''</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: For <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(x) = 4x^3 - x + 7</annotation></semantics></math>, what is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">‴</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p'''(x)</annotation></semantics></math>?
